title: Minimum Cost to Reach Destination in Time
summary: In a country with n cities connected by bi-directional roads, each road has a travel time.
statement: In a country with n cities connected by bi-directional roads, each road has a travel time. You must pay a passing fee for each city visited. Starting from city 0, you aim to reach city n-1 within a given time limit. The cost is the sum of passing fees for all cities visited. Determine the minimum cost or return -1 if the journey is impossible within the time limit.
constraints: 1 <= max_time <= 1000; there are 2 through 1000 cities and at most 1000 undirected weighted edges.
Pay a city's fee every time it is visited, including start and destination.
Return minimum fee among walks reaching the last city within max_time, or -1 when impossible.
hints: Time is a bounded integer resource, so use dynamic programming over exact elapsed time and current city.
For each time, relax both directions of every edge from the state at time minus its travel duration.
Take the minimum destination cost over all elapsed times up to max_time.
Every feasible walk ends with some edge and smaller exact-time state, so the recurrence covers all walks; minimizing each state preserves the cheapest one.
editorial: Every feasible walk ends with some edge and smaller exact-time state, so the recurrence covers all walks; minimizing each state preserves the cheapest one.

tests.explanation: The 0-1-2-5 path takes thirty minutes and costs 5+1+2+3 = 11.
The cheap route is too slow, so the faster 0-3-4-5 route costs 48.
